review.scope: Bounded work-specific doctrinal sampling and acquisition. No exhaustive human review, global registry approval or owner selection of a covenant model.

decisions.author: Benjamin Keach

evidence.locator: Held short confession: Trinity; Scriptures; Christ Mediator; humiliation/exaltation; justification; resurrection
evidence.finding: Explicit six-anchor confidence, including one essence/three persons, two natures/one Christ, satisfaction in our place, third-day resurrection, faith alone and authoritative Scriptures.
Water baptism, immersion, credible believers, death/burial/resurrection sign and strict communion argument checked against the offered body.
1689 identity, existing keyboarded diplomatic transcription and CC0 are explicit; all 14 chapter divisions present.

limits: Two witnesses, not two works. Modern PDF omits some footnotes and modernizes wording/heading/reference presentation.
TCP has 225 encoded gaps; source damage/substitute pages are documented. No critical-edition or character-perfect claim.
Strict-communion and polemical assertions remain Keach-specific; historical lexical claims require source checking.
Modern editor foreword/image are not Keach doctrine. PDF describes its base as automatic transcription; TCP describes keyboarding/review. Preserve both provenance statements.

decisions.author: Abraham Booth

evidence.locator: Held Reign of Grace: election discussion, chapters 6, 11, 12 and 13
evidence.finding: Six-anchor confidence: three distinct divine persons, Scripture as only faith/practice rule, divine/human Mediator, substitution/satisfaction, resurrection and justification through Christ received by faith rather than works.
Defence of baptism obligation and refusing Table communion to paedobaptist believers; not a universal Baptist communion rule.

evidence.locator: 1829 title/third-edition advertisement and general contents; volumes I-III
evidence.finding: Three-volume edition includes baptism treatise plus replies to Williams/Edwards. All three offered texts verified, not the misleading one-volume church PDF.

limits: Booth is the arguing author; opponent extracts and ancient/modern witnesses are attributed quotations, never endorsed as independent source teaching.
James Dore preface and 1829 third-edition advertisement/index have separate contributor roles; publisher advertisements are not theology.
Apology footnote130 explicitly added by modern editor; original and editor statements must remain distinct.

Existing archive OCR has damaged words/Greek/headings; volume III CHATTER VI is an OCR error, annotated only. Historical church-history/lexical quotations are study evidence, not independently verified facts.

decisions.author: John Spilsbury

evidence.finding: Explicit Trinity, divine/human Son, death satisfying justice for elect, resurrection in same body, faith in Christ righteousness alone and Scripture sole authority.
Covenant/approved subjects, restoration of ordinances and covenant forming church before baptism are source-specific arguments.

limits: Canonical author spelling Spilsbury; historic title spells Spilsbery. This is enlarged 1652, not silently first-edition 1643.
Article7 rejects a generalized grace/salvation offer; preserve and flag for comparison with Dagg/Fuller, not default contemporary evangelism teaching.
Antichrist polemic and restoration/succession claims are historical argument requiring contextual assessment, not blanket approval of host Landmark views.
Modern editor changes spelling/case/Scripture reference format; disclosed pp.2-3.

decisions.author: Rexford Semrad

evidence.finding: Primary institutional declaration fully subscribing and maintaining teaching fidelity to the 1689; 1689 chapters 1 (Scripture), 2 (Trinity), 8 (divine/human Mediator, substitution and resurrection), 11/14 (grace and faith-alone justification), 31 (bodily resurrection).

evidence.locator: Selected complete article/series with named byline
evidence.finding: Actual articles represent CBTS, call the 1689 our confession and argue its covenant/works language. The 2020 article rejects making 1689 Federalism a necessary condition of full subscription.

limits: Do not turn institutional affiliation into blanket author approval. Claims about historic majority are Semrad attributed assessments; no complete history independently checked.

decisions.author: Sam Waldron

evidence.finding: Primary institutional declaration fully subscribing and maintaining teaching fidelity to the 1689; 1689 chapters 1 (Scripture), 2 (Trinity), 8 (divine/human Mediator, substitution and resurrection), 11/14 (grace and faith-alone justification), 31 (bodily resurrection).

evidence.locator: Selected complete article/series with named byline
evidence.finding: Named president in primary about page; full 2026 essay now identifies New Covenant with Covenant of Grace while affirming salvation under OT by promised Christ. All 3 baptism lessons contain publisher disagreement disclaimer.

limits: 2026 self-statement supersedes simplistic camp labels drawn from 2020 summaries. Neither child-age policy nor every system detail is a uniform CBTS position.
The professing-child series is not infant baptism. Its legal/cultural age examples are dated illustrations, not current legal advice or imposed church policy.

evidence.finding: Primary institutional declaration fully subscribing and maintaining teaching fidelity to the 1689; 1689 chapters 1 (Scripture), 2 (Trinity), 8 (divine/human Mediator, substitution and resurrection), 11/14 (grace and faith-alone justification), 31 (bodily resurrection).

evidence.locator: Selected complete article/series with named byline
evidence.finding: Article identifies author as CBTS professor and Grace Reformed Baptist pastor; actual body uses 1689 30:1,30:7 and catechism94,97 to distinguish spiritual feeding by faith from automatic sacramental effect.

decisions.author: Daniel Scheiderer

evidence.finding: Site explicitly states its authors views consistent with 1677/89 confession; names author and Reformed Baptist seminary roles. 1689 chapters 1 (Scripture), 2 (Trinity), 8 (divine/human Mediator, substitution and resurrection), 11/14 (grace and faith-alone justification), 31 (bodily resurrection).

evidence.locator: Second London Covenant Theology; Intersections; Divergences; Keeping Dialogue
evidence.finding: Source affirms confession and compares creation/works, natural/positive law, Decalogue and Sabbath with progressive covenantalism.

limits: Progressive covenantalism is a conservative Baptist system, not a progressive/liberal denomination; this collected article is a confessional assessment of it.
Do not adopt progressive covenantalism as a default 1689 model. A primary progressive-covenantalist full article remains link-only because collector access failed.
Scheiderer is the bylined author, not all listed Baptist Dogmatics contributors jointly. Claims about another system are attributed comparison, not a neutral adjudication.
